title: Trade Apgar -- pre-trade go/no-go scoring (ch. 58)
description: Ch. 58's pre-trade Trade Apgar: a 5-question, 0-2-each go/no-go score (>=7 total, no single zero) tied to a named strategy -- the pre-trade counterpart to ch.55's after-the-fact grading. Elder's own example strategy's five questions: weekly Impulse, daily Impulse, daily price-vs-value, false-breakout status, and 'perfection' (both timeframes look ideal). Three of these five inputs are data this app already computes for any ticker (weekly/daily Impulse from analyse()'s screens output; price-vs-value from the existing EMA13/EMA26 value zone) -- this task should auto-populate those rather than rebuilding them, per docs/ideas.md's own sizing note. Depends on backend-trade-strategy-tagging since a Trade Apgar is inherently strategy-specific (Elder: 'the scoring method you're about to see is designed for one system... all other systems will require a different test').

checklist.step: Decide the data model for a first version: a fixed 5-question set matching Elder's own example strategy, versus a per-strategy configurable question set -- record the rationale (a configurable system is the 'real' long-term shape but a fixed set matching the book's own example is a reasonable, much smaller first version).
Implement auto-population of the weekly Impulse, daily Impulse, and price-vs-value-zone questions from the existing analyse() pipeline for a given ticker.

Leave false-breakout-status and 'perfection' as manual inputs for this first version; decide whether to surface kangaroo_tail/support_resistance output as a suggested (not authoritative) starting value for the false-breakout question, and record the decision.
Implement the go/no-go scoring rule: sum >= 7 AND no single question scored 0.

Unit tests covering auto-populated fields for a real ticker fixture, manual-field handling, and the go/no-go threshold logic including the 'no single zero' rule specifically (a trade scoring 8 total but with one zero must still fail).
